text:
Sam R.: Hey team, tenant acme-ml is getting ~20% 504s on hosted API since 11:12Z. Customers seeing streaming timeouts and partial tokens. Example request id: req-0a1b2c3d. Can someone triage?

Maya P.: Thanks — can you paste a failing curl and any x-request-id/x-envoy headers? Also which model route?

Sam R.: sure. endpoint: POST /v1/generate?model=gpt-large-hosted

curl -i -X POST 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate?model=gpt-large-hosted' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDACTED' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"input":"hello"}'

Response (failing):
HTTP/2 504
x-request-id: req-0a1b2c3d
x-envoy-upstream-service-time: 12011
content-type: application/json
{"message":"upstream request timed out"}

Josh K.: That x-envoy-upstream-service-time ~12s is a smoking gun. I suspect the billing/auth validate call (synchronous price check) is blocking upstream. Saw similar pattern last month when billing sync spiked. Can we grab edge envoy logs and the billing service latency graph?

infra-bot: [alert] prod/edge: 11:10Z -> 11:18Z increased 5xx rate for route /v1/generate (hosted) - p95 latency up 800ms -> 4200ms. CPU spike on billing-validate pods + increased error rate.

Eli (oncall): I'm on it. Sam, can you run this kibana query and paste first 50 lines?

Query: 
service:edge AND route:"/v1/generate" AND trace.id:req-0a1b2c3d

Sam R.: pasted top lines from envoy (trimmed):
```
[11:12:07.123] envoy error: upstream response timeout, upstream_host=10.4.12.5:443, x-request-id=req-0a1b2c3d
[11:12:07.124] envoy info: response_duration_ms=12011 route=gpt-large-hosted
[11:12:07.125] envoy warn: connection reset while proxying to upstream billing-validate-0.acme.svc.cluster.local:50443
```

Maya P.: That reset + huge upstream time aligns w/ billing-validate pod GC/DB stall. If billing blocks, auth path waits and edge hits its 10s upstream timeout -> 504. Two prongs: mitigation (quick) and fix (billing scaling/cache).

Josh K.: Quick mitigation options: 1) enable short-circuit auth cache for acme-ml (serve from cache TTL while billing returns slow); 2) bump edge upstream timeout to 20s for that tenant route; 3) route traffic to a fallback model variant with lower billing hits. I prefer #1 + #3.

Eli (oncall): I'll apply a temporary routing override to send acme-ml traffic to gpt-large-hosted-fallback and enable cached-auth. Patching now. @Maya please prep rollback plan.

Eli (oncall): ran patch: 
```
kubectl -n edge patch configmap tenant-routes --type=json -p '[{"op":"add","path":"/acme-ml/override","value":{"route":"gpt-large-hosted-fallback","auth_cache":true,"auth_cache_ttl":300}}]'
```

infra-bot: routing-override applied for tenant acme-ml (id: override-1712345678) — 2s ago.

Sam R.: Customer reports 504s dropped to <1% within 90s. Confirmed streaming resumed. :thumbsup:

Maya P.: Nice. For next steps: 1) create ticket to add circuit-breaker+retry for billing-validate (SRE#4567), 2) increase billing-validate HPA and investigate DB slow queries, 3) add per-tenant alert for billing latency > 500ms. I'll own follow-up.

Josh K.: Add note to run an offline eval of auth-cache correctness for edge fallback (ensure no PII leakage). Also schedule a deploy of the cached-auth feature to reduce manual patches.

Eli (oncall): Logged incident 2026-03-17-ACME-504, assigned to SRE and Billing. I'm leaving the override for 1h and will monitor. If no regression, we keep until fix merged.

Sam R.: closing loop with customer: replied with status and temporary workaround. Will escalate if they see any regression. Thanks all.

Maya P.: action items -> SRE#4567 (billing HPA + DB), DEV#7890 (cached-auth feature), ALERT#1011 (per-tenant billing latency).

Josh K.: thx, doing a quick postmortem draft.

Eli (oncall): marking thread resolved for now, will reopen if metrics bump back up.
